claims.event: Liao jinshi made resident commissioner of the Southern Capital; he killed Zuo Qigong and others, defected to the Song, and was executed by the Song with his head sent to the Jin.
Surrendered Ping Prefecture and warned in his memorial about forced relocations.
Took Yanjing, ceded it to the Song, and issued an edict to the Southern Capital officials.
Sent with Xiebo to admonish Zhang Jue with an imperial edict.
Killed under the chestnut grove on Zhang Jue's orders while passing Ping Prefecture toward Guangning.
Killed under the chestnut grove on Zhang Jue's orders while passing Ping Prefecture toward Guangning.
Killed under the chestnut grove on Zhang Jue's orders while passing Ping Prefecture toward Guangning.
Killed under the chestnut grove on Zhang Jue's orders while passing Ping Prefecture toward Guangning.
Marched from Jin Prefecture, twice routed Zhang Jue, but was badly defeated at Rabbit-Ear Mountain.
Promoted by the Song to Huayou Pavilion academician along with Zhang Jue's followers.
Took the Southern Capital and demanded the Song surrender Zhang Jue.
Hid Zhang Jue in the armory, offered a lookalike head, and finally produced him.
Feared he would be demanded next after Zhang Jue was handed over.
Managed the Inner Treasury and palace works for Shizong, irrigated fields at Taining Palace, became Commissioner for Encouraging Agriculture, and was posthumously honored.
Found the infant Zhang Jinyan when Pingshan fell and raised him at home.
Adored the boy Jinyan and took him to be presented to Empress Zhenyi.
Received the boy Jinyan and kept him at the princely residence.
Was acclaimed emperor at Dongjing with Jinyan urging him, and relied on Jinyan while denying him real power.
Campaigned in Jiang and Huai and died at Yangzhou.
As Minister of Rites helped dispose of palace stores at Nanjing after Hailing's death.
Her tomb construction was directed by Zhang Jinyan.
Served sixteen years in the Palace Parks Office and was called an honest household servant by the emperor.

claims.statement: Executed by the Song and his head sent to the Jin.
Died of illness; the emperor sent officials to perform funeral rites.

claims.event: Punished Yinshuge and Xiyin for delay, summoned Yudu by edict after taking Linhuang, and ordered Yudu's family guarded.
His column was attacked by Yudu while crossing the Liao River.
Liao clansman who surrendered to the Jin with his officers, led victories against the Song near Taiyuan, later plotted rebellion and was killed by border forces.
Camped with Yudu at the Hun River and fled before Yinshuge arrived.
Opposed Yudu at the Hun River and was punished by Taizu for delay.
Opposed Yudu at the Hun River and was punished by Taizu for delay.
Surrendered Longhua Prefecture to the Jin and expelled Tabuye.
Made military commissioner of Longhua by the Liao and expelled by Zhang Yinggu.
Held the rear at the Liao River and repelled Yudu, taking five hundred armored horses.
Surrendered to the Jin together with Yudu as one of his officers.
Surrendered to the Jin together with Yudu as one of his officers.
Surrendered to the Jin together with Yudu as one of his officers.
Sent by Yudu to record and report offices, households and livestock.

Mother of the Prince of Jin, whom Yudu thought should be heir.
Esteemed eldest son of Consort Wen; plotted with Yixin and Yudu without success.
Agreed with Yudu from the previous spring to defect to the Jin.
Moved with Delidi to strike against Yudu.
Took the Central Capital with Yudu as guide.
Former wine superintendent nominated by Yudu as military commissioner of Fengsheng.
Resettled over three thousand residents and was promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
Prefectural clerk nominated as observation commissioner of Fengsheng.
Accused Yudu, Wu Shi and Liu La of plotting rebellion.
Accused by Yelu Mazhe of plotting rebellion with Yudu.
Accused by Yelu Mazhe of plotting rebellion with Yudu.
Was flogged seventy strokes over the alleged plot.
Captured by Yudu north of the Fen while relieving Taiyuan.

Captured by Yudu north of the Fen while relieving Taiyuan.

Received a titular frontier military commission as reward for exposing Yudu.
Followed Saba's revolt, then killed Saba and took his forces.
Led a Khitan revolt and was killed by Yila Wowa.

claims.statement: Killed with his sons by border forces, his head sent to court.
Put to death as Yudu's ally.

Mobilized troops against the Song, drafting the Khitan, and sent Pusan Hutu to crush the revolt.
Chancellor Gushen prophesied that the northwestern tribes would one day rise.
Killed Saba, made himself supreme commander, besieged Linhuang and proclaimed himself emperor with era Tianzheng.
Former interpreter who led the Khitan revolt, headed west toward Dashi, and was killed by Yila Wowa and Chen Jia.
Sent to draft the Khitan, dared not relay their plea, and was killed by the rebels.
Sent to draft the Khitan and died of anxiety.
Pressed the Northwestern Circuit draft and was taken prisoner by the rebels.
Pressed the Northwestern Circuit draft and was taken prisoner by the rebels.
Revolted with Saba and was later seized by Yila Wowa.
Rebels debated enthroning one of his descendants.
Commandant raised by rebels as pacification commissioner, later taken prisoner by Wowa.

Pasture commissioner killed by the Khitan rebels.
Killed military commissioner Shujiawuzhe to join Saba's revolt.

Rebelled at Xianping, took Han Prefecture, was routed at Xin Prefecture and joined Saba.
Tried to arrest Kuoluo's family and was defeated.

Sent to suppress the revolt and executed for sluggish pursuit.

Sent to offer terms to Wowa and returned.

As deputy commander of elite cavalry led the cavalry wing against Wowa.
Feinted across the Mengjing River, fought on with an arrow in his arm, and was made right army supervisor.

Recalled to the capital from the campaign against Wowa.
Chased the rebels fifteen li and had his men dismount to shoot when the rebels counterattacked.

Killed when he went back into rebel territory to bring out his family.

claims.statement: Died before taking office in Jian Prefecture.

Wowa's mother, who fled west from Luoguo Ridge and was run down by Zhining.
